problem: End-to-end VLM navigation agents rely on 2D RGB observations and lack explicit 3D spatial awareness, so they fail in spatially intricate, cluttered scenes. Depth/LiDAR only see visible surfaces, and occupancy methods from driving use VQ-VAE discrete codebooks that do not generalize to heterogeneous indoor/outdoor embodied layouts.
motivation: 3D occupancy gives a holistic volumetric representation that supports both high-level grounding and low-level collision avoidance, including amodal completion of occluded space. It can be predicted from RGB alone, which scales better than scanning. The authors observe that discrete VQ tokens lose information in unstructured scenes, and that a navigation policy mostly needs coarse spatial cues. This suggests a single compact continuous token could carry the spatial prior cheaply inside a VLM.
key_idea: Train a Qwen3-VL-based navigation model to first predict one continuous 'spatial token', supervised by decoding it into local 3D occupancy via a pre-trained (de-quantized) VQ-VAE decoder, then feed that token back as a spatial chain-of-thought step before regressing trajectory waypoints, co-trained across VLN, urban and point-goal tasks.
insight: Explicit occupancy supervision plus conditioning the action on the predicted spatial token is what drives the gains. On the InternVLA-N1 S1 point-goal benchmark (Home/Commercial SR), results are: full model 90.9/91.0; w/o occupancy 70.5/75.1; w/o spatial CoT (occupancy only as an auxiliary task) 81.3/85.2; discrete VQ tokens 80.3/80.0 with IoU 45.03 vs 58.11. Train-test consistency is the most critical factor: skipping Stage II (student-forcing on self-predicted tokens after teacher-forcing on GT occupancy) collapses SR to 56.8/67.3 despite nearly identical IoU (58.04), which is worse than using no occupancy at all. A single token is enough: going from 150 tokens to 1 costs only marginal IoU, gives +26% FPS and equal or slightly better SR. CoT slightly lowers IoU (60.71→58.11) because the token learns navigation-critical abstractions (e.g., chairs as holistic obstacles) rather than fine geometry. Spatial awareness also transfers across tasks: the 'Generalize' variant, trained with no VLN occupancy labels, still beats prior SOTA on R2R-CE/RxR-CE.
method: Observation encoding: the Qwen3-VL vision encoder and projector process multi-view RGB video. NavFoM-style spatiotemporal compression probabilistically samples a fixed number of history frames and average-pools their features. These are concatenated with full-resolution current-frame features.

Encoder-Decoder (ED) initialization: a VQ-VAE occupancy tokenizer (2D ResNet-UNet treating the height axis as channels) is pre-trained on the large occupancy dataset with BCE + Lovász-hinge + VQ commitment losses. Its encoder and decoder are reused in SPAN-Nav.

Compact continuous spatial token: quantization is discarded and the continuous latent z_t is used. Proj_O2H compresses dense occupancy latents into a single VLM input token. Proj_H2O maps the VLM output hidden state back to occupancy latent space. Supervision is L_occ (BCE + Lovász on the decoded occupancy grid) plus L_latent (MSE to Enc(O_GT)).

Spatial Chain-of-Thought action reasoning: the VLM first predicts the spatial token, re-injects it via Proj_O2H, then produces an action hidden state. An MLP action head regresses M egocentric waypoints (x, y, θ), trained with L2 loss against GT trajectories.

Two-stage training with QA co-training: Stage I uses teacher forcing with GT-occupancy latents (L_occ + L_latent + L_act + L_qa) on 2M occupancy-annotated trajectories plus 0.5M QA. Stage II uses student forcing on self-predicted tokens over the full mixed data (L_occ + L_act + L_qa), with L_occ zeroed where no GT occupancy exists.

Occupancy/trajectory data engine: Isaac Sim voxelization (0.05×0.05×0.1 m voxels; 4 m front, 2 m behind, 2 m each side) over 1091 InteriorGS + MP3D scenes. Real-world labels for FrodoBots-2K come from Depth Anything 3 reconstruction, RANSAC ground removal and ray casting. Point-goal trajectories come from an A* + truncated Velocity-Obstacle planner. FrodoBots trajectories are rebuilt via wheel-encoder dead reckoning with ZUPT, Kalman filtering and RTS smoothing.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL (fine-tuned end-to-end) + VQ-VAE-initialized occupancy encoder/decoder (quantizer dropped) + 2 projectors + MLP action head
setting.training_data: 7.08M samples in total: 5.08M trajectories, 0.93M image QA and 1.07M video QA. Trajectories: VLN 1.8M from VLN-CE R2R/RxR incl. a DAgger round; urban navigation 1.28M from MetaUrban sim plus real-world Sekai and FrodoBots-2K with HTL lifting; point-goal 2M in 1,000 InteriorGS scenes via an A*+VO planner. 4.2M occupancy annotations from Isaac Sim (InteriorGS + MP3D, 1091 scenes) and Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-labels on FrodoBots-2K. Stage I: 2M occupancy-annotated trajectories + 0.5M QA; Stage II: full data. Trained on 32 H100 for about 1 day (768 GPU-h).

setting.action_space: predicted local trajectory of M egocentric waypoints (x, y, θ), executed by embodiment-specific local planners/controllers
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE R2R/RxR), MetaUrban, Isaac Sim (InternScenes / InternVLA-N1 S1 point-goal benchmark; occupancy annotation)

results: With RGB only, SPAN-Nav reaches 66.3 SR / 59.3 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 69.7 SR / 60.1 SPL / 67.9 nDTW on RxR-CE val-unseen. This beats the prior SOTA NavFoM (61.7 / 64.4 SR) by 4.6 / 5.3 points despite fewer training samples (7.08M vs 12.7M), and also beats RGB-D + odometry methods such as HNR and ETPNav. On MetaUrban it matches or exceeds UrbanVLA's SR while cutting collision cost by over 4× (e.g., 0.22 vs 0.94 on PointNav test; SNS 96 vs 87). On the InternVLA-N1 S1 point-goal benchmark it scores 90.9 / 91.0 SR (Home / Commercial) vs 60.0 / 71.4 for the RGB-D InternVLA-N1 S1.
limitations: Requires large-scale 3D occupancy supervision (4.2M labels from Isaac Sim reconstructions or Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-labels); real-world labels are noisy pseudo-GT, and the local occupancy window is fixed (4 m front / 2 m back / 2 m sides).

Real-world evaluation is only qualitative, runs on a remote RTX 4090 server rather than onboard, and uses LiDAR as a safety fallback in crowded areas; point-goal and MetaUrban evaluations use specific embodiments (Dingo, wheelchair).
Cross-embodiment generalization (different kinematics/sensor layouts) is left to future work, and the model size and some details (token-count results) are not reported numerically.
